title: The price of one degree
subtitle: The same small bend, read at two distances.
note: The angle is drawn far larger than one degree. At true scale the two lines could not be told apart on this page.
caption: Reading the figure: the bend is the same at every point on the line. What changes with distance is how easy it is to see and what it costs to correct.
panels: About two inches off. One person, one shovel, before lunch.
Cheap to fix. Hard to see.
About ninety feet off. A different trench, with a year of work in it.
Easy to see. Expensive to fix.

title: Three forms, and what is behind each
subtitle: The shapes are the ones the first paper drew. The forces are what a company can act on.
note: None of the three is healthy or unhealthy in itself. Each has a version a company can live with and one that costs it dearly.
caption: Reading the figure: the shapes are the ones the first paper drew. What this paper adds is the force behind each one, because the force is what a company can act on.
panels: Held by a pull from outside, a person, a rule, or upkeep.
Bent by rewards that overlap: the same customer, market, budget, or credit.
Bent by customers, measures, and clocks that differ.

title: How converging grows
subtitle: Five stages. The question changes between the second and the third.
note: A question about the work can be settled by looking at the work. A question about ownership gets settled by power.
caption: Reading the figure: the question changes between the second stage and the third, from who does the work better to who owns it. Before that change a fix is usually cheaper. After it the price can rise sharply.
panels: The same work, done twice. Neither group knows.
The two groups meet. Often the cheapest moment there will be.
The question changes from who does it better to who owns it.
The rival is a colleague. The sensible moves point inward.
A ruling from the top, or two of everything for years.

title: How diverging grows
subtitle: Five stages. Nothing collides at any of them.
note: Each step apart makes each division’s own work a little easier, so nobody inside complains.
caption: Reading the figure: nothing collides at any stage, which is why diverging tends to be found late, and often from outside.
panels: Each division tunes itself to its own customers.
Its own calendar, its own systems, its own words.
The company plan is the divisions’ plans in one binder.
People work for the division, not the company.
Under one roof, and sometimes competing.

title: Reading the three forms
subtitle: What is behind each one, what it shows early and late, and what separates its two versions.
note: In every column the early signs are where a company may still have a cheaper choice.
caption: Reading the figure: each column runs from cause to test. The early signs are small enough to miss, which is why someone has to be looking for them.
panels: What is behind it: A pull from outside, a person, a rule, or upkeep.
Early signs: Two division heads, asked separately, give different answers about what the company is trying to do.
Late signs: The thing holding the lines goes, the trenches bend, and the company blames the newest thing it can find.
What separates the two versions: Whether anyone can say what is holding the lines, and what happens when it goes.
What is behind it: Rewards that overlap.
Early signs: A tool built twice. A job posted twice. A sale counted twice. A customer called twice.
Late signs: Scheming, infighting, turf wars. Every question of ownership goes to the top.
What separates the two versions: Whether someone above both knew, decided what it was for, set a rule for how it ends, and paid neither side for the other’s failure.
What is behind it: Customers, measures, and clocks that differ.
Early signs: People stop moving between divisions. One word means two things. Exceptions to company rules.
Late signs: Two contracts for one customer. The parts are valued at more than the whole.
What separates the two versions: Whether someone decided the division may go its own way, said how far, and keeps asking what the parts still do together.
